teaser.text: Cummins sells the machinery that makes vehicles move, keeps industrial equipment running and supplies electricity when buildings need it. Its business begins with an engine or component, but the dollar moves through manufacturers, distributors, service networks and customers over the equipment’s life.

stock.opening: Cummins's weighted price is $521.64 in October 2027, with 25% bear, 55% base and 20% bull probabilities. Cummins's forecast hinges on Power Systems capacity converting into shipments and cash.
stock.closing: The full memo also explains Cummins's business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: Where could Cummins's shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: At today’s $531.33, the weighted price is $521.64 in October 2027. Including dividends, that is roughly flat. It rises to $589.37 in October 2028, a 14% total return. By October 2029, it reaches $681.25, a 34% return. The 2029 range runs from $315.70 in the bear case to $1,087.31 in the bull case. The forecast assigns 25% to the bear, 55% to the base and 20% to the bull, reflecting a cyclical business with credible growth but substantial execution risk.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for Cummins's base case, and what could go wrong?

paragraphs.text: Operating profit is the main earnings choice. The base case rises from $5,000 million in October 2027 to $5,800 million in October 2029. It assumes revenue grows from the 2026 guided level, Power Systems capacity converts into shipments and trucks recover gradually, with normal-cycle margins near 12.8%–13.4%. The bear case stays near $4,000 million because truck weakness, delayed generators and launch costs arrive first. The bull reaches $6,800 million as data-center orders convert quickly and margins approach 14%. Power Systems sales rose 19% in the latest quarter, but Engine sales fell 7% and its EBITDA fell faster, supporting both sides of the range.
The bear case requires delayed data-center projects, underused new capacity, a weaker truck cycle and costly launches.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Cummins really make?

paragraphs.text: Free cash flow means operating cash flow after capital spending on factories and equipment. Stock compensation does not consume current cash, but it gives employees an economic claim, so subtracting it produces a stricter owner-oriented measure.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for Cummins today?

paragraphs.text: Market value is what shareholders’ ownership is worth. Enterprise value goes further: it approximates the cost of buying the operating business while taking responsibility for its borrowings. Cummins had $7,695 million of debt and $3,924 million of cash and marketable securities in June 2026, leaving $3,771 million of net debt. The balance sheet also included $1,059 million belonging to owners of consolidated subsidiaries other than Cummins shareholders.

dividend.title: Cummins dividend
dividend.meta_description: Cummins pays a growing dividend, but cash coverage has varied; the full memo follows the cash, outlook and yield.
dividend.opening: Cummins pays a dividend that has risen for 17 consecutive years; the forecast's base case increases it from $9.18 per share to $10.48 by 2029. Cummins' cash coverage has varied: free cash flow was $279 million against $969 million of dividends in 2024, then reached $2,386 million in 2025.
dividend.closing: The full memo also explains Cummins' business, rivals, management decisions and risks.

blocks.heading: How much does Cummins pay per share over the years shown?

paragraphs.text: Dividends rise from $9.18 per share in the base case to $10.48 by 2029. The bear holds at $8.80 through 2028 before reaching $9.24, while the bull reaches $11.30. The latest quarterly increase was 10%, and Cummins has raised its dividend for 17 consecutive years. Strong 2025 free cash flow supports continued growth, but the 2024 cash-flow shortfall argues against assuming uninterrupted increases.

blocks.heading: Does Cummins' dividend fit its free cash flow?

paragraphs.text: The 2024 cash squeeze came from the emissions settlement. Cummins recorded the charge in 2023, when the obligation became measurable, but paid $1.9 billion in 2024 after the settlement became final. Free cash flow fell to $279 million while dividends remained $969 million. The timing matters: earnings can absorb a charge before the cash bill arrives.

Cash recovered in 2025. Free cash flow reached $2,386 million, acquisitions absorbed only $12 million, and net debt declined to $3,943 million as cash and short-term investments increased. Power-generation capacity has the strongest recent operating evidence: management said completed capacity was supporting growth and that customers wanted more equipment than suppliers could deliver. Hydrogen has the weakest evidence, because repeated write-downs preceded the retreat.

paragraphs.text: Cummins makes engines, power-generation equipment and components, then earns more by servicing them. At $531.33 a share, its stock says that stronger profits are coming—and that they must last.

earnings.title: Cummins earnings: guidance and next results
earnings.meta_description: Cummins expects results on November 5, 2026; see its guidance, recent performance and what to watch.
earnings.opening: Cummins is expected to report results on November 5, 2026. Watch whether generator equipment is shipped and paid for, while truck growth preserves margins.
earnings.closing: The full memo also answers how Cummins makes money, who its rivals are, how its management is judged, and what risks it faces.

paragraphs.text: Management guides to 2026 revenue growth of 10.0%–13.0% and an EBITDA margin of 18.0%–18.5%. Power Systems revenue is guided to grow 14.0%–19.0%. Accelera is guided to lose $260 million–$290 million of EBITDA.

blocks.heading: Has Cummins kept its past promises?

paragraphs.text: The committee raised Davis’s annual payout from 80% to 90%, citing slower adoption. It also raised her three-year performance-share payout from 50% to 110%, citing market and policy effects. Shareholders faced those conditions too. Adjusting targets after disappointment can weaken the promise that incentives reward results set in advance.

blocks.heading: What do Cummins’s last eight quarters show?

paragraphs.text: Revenue rose 9.4% from the prior-year quarter, while net income and diluted earnings per share rose more slowly. Gross margin, operating margin and EBITDA margin all declined. Cummins therefore sold more without retaining quite as much of each sales dollar.

blocks.heading: What should you watch in Cummins’s next release?

paragraphs.text: The nearest test is the November 5, 2026 earnings call. Investors should look for generator equipment shipped and paid for, not merely stronger orders, and for truck growth that preserves margins.

The engine launches provide a second test. Cummins plans limited production of the X10 and X15 in January 2027, followed by full production later in the year. The B platform follows in January 2028. These launches require certification, suppliers, factories and truck makers to move together.
